message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling *detailed* information about a network interface (e.g., eth0, enp3s0, wlan0) on the three major desktop/server families. Feel free to copy/paste the snippets into your terminal or adapt them for scripts. --- ## 1️⃣ Linux / Unix / macOS (BSD‑style) | Command | What it shows | Typical output | |---------|---------------|----------------| | `ip link show ` | Interface state, MAC, MTU, flags | `2: enp3s0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000` | | `ip addr show ` | IP addresses, netmask, broadcast, scope | `inet 192.168.1.10/24 brd 192.168.1.255 scope global dynamic noprefixroute enp3s0` | | `ethtool ` | Driver, speed, duplex, autoneg, driver version | `Settings for enp3s0:`
` Supported ports: [ TP ]`
` Supported link modes: ...` | | `ethtool -S ` | Driver statistics counters | `rx_packets: 1234567`
`tx_errors: 0` | | `cat /sys/class/net//statistics/*` | Raw counter values | `rx_bytes: 987654321` | | `lshw -class network -short` | Hardware description (requires root) | `*-network description: Ethernet interface` | | `nmcli device show ` | NetworkManager view (Ubuntu, Fedora) | `GENERAL.DEVICE: enp3s0` | **Example** – Pull all details at once: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash IFACE=${1:-eth0} echo "=== $IFACE ===" ip link show "$IFACE" ip addr show "$IFACE" ethtool "$IFACE" ethtool -S "$IFACE" | head -n 20 # first 20 stats ``` --- ## 2️⃣ Windows (PowerShell) | Cmdlet | What it shows | Example | |--------|---------------|---------| | `Get-NetAdapter -Name ""` | Adapter status, MAC, speed, media type | `Name : Ethernet0`
`Status : Up`
`MacAddress : 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E` | | `Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias ""` | IP config | `IPAddress : 192.168.1.10`
`PrefixLength : 24` | | `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias ""` | Full config + DNS | `IPv4DefaultGateway : 192.168.1.1` | | `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name ""` | Advanced settings | `DisplayName : Speed & Duplex`
`Value : 100 Mbps Full Duplex` | | `Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter -Filter "NetConnectionID=''"` | WMI view (older) | `MACAddress : 001A2B3C4D5E` | **Example** – PowerShell one‑liner: ```powershell $iface='Ethernet' Get-NetAdapter -Name $iface | Format-List * Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $iface | Format-Table AddressFamily, IPAddress, PrefixLength, DefaultGateway ``` --- ## 3️⃣ macOS (Darwin) | Command | What it shows | Example | |---------|---------------|---------| | `ifconfig ` | Flags, MAC, IP, netmask, broadcast | `en0: flags=8863 mtu 1500` | | `networksetup -getinfo ` | Service name, IP, subnet mask, router | `IP address: 192.168.1.10` | | `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType -detailLevel full` | Full hardware + software profile | Search for `` section | | `scutil --dns` | DNS configuration | `nameserver[0] : 8.8.8.8` | --- ## 4️⃣ SNMP (for remote devices) If you have SNMP enabled on the target, you can pull interface data via OIDs: | OID | Description | Tool | |-----|-------------|------| | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.` | ifIndex | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifIndex` | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.` | ifDescr | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifDescr` | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.` | ifOperStatus | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16.` | ifInOctets | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifInOctets` | | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.17.` | ifOutOctets | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifOutOctets` | **Python example** (using pysnmp): ```python from pysnmp.hlapi import * def snmp_walk(host, community, oid): for (errorIndication, errorStatus, errorIndex, varBinds) in nextCmd(SnmpEngine(), CommunityData(community), UdpTransportTarget((host, 161)), ContextData(), ObjectType(ObjectIdentity(oid))): if errorIndication: print(errorIndication) break elif errorStatus: print('%s at %s' % (errorStatus.prettyPrint(), errorIndex and varBinds[int(errorIndex)-1][0] or '?')) break else: for varBind in varBinds: print(' = '.join([x.prettyPrint() for x in varBind])) snmp_walk('192.168.1.1', 'public', '1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2') ``` --- ## 5️⃣ Programmatic Retrieval (Python subprocess) If you prefer to wrap the native utilities in a script: ```python import subprocess, json, shlex def run(cmd): return subprocess.check_output(shlex.split(cmd)).decode().strip() def iface_details(iface='eth0'): out = { 'link': run(f'ip link show {iface}'), 'addr': run(f'ip addr show {iface}'), 'ethtool': run(f'ethtool {iface}'), 'stats': run(f'ethtool -S {iface}') } return out print(json.dumps(iface_details(), indent=2)) ``` --- ### Quick Checklist | ✅ | Item | Why it matters | |---|------|----------------| | `ip link` | Link state, carrier, MTU | Detect physical link loss | | `ip addr` | IP config | Verify correct addressing | | `ethtool` | Driver, speed, duplex | Confirm negotiated link parameters | | `ethtool -S` | Counters | Baseline traffic, errors | | `/sys/class/net/.../statistics` | Raw counters | For high‑resolution monitoring | | SNMP | Remote polling | For network‑wide dashboards | Pick the set that matches your environment and plug it into your monitoring or troubleshooting workflow!
